original_title: Blake Snell exits Dodgers' loss early because of injury
original_body:
Blake Snell exits Dodgers’ loss early because of injury
-    Click here to listen to this article
-   
CINCINNATI — The trouble started as Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell threw in the Great American Ball Park bullpen before the game.
“I felt good all day, and then the second-to-last pitch of the bullpen, I threw a slider and then I felt it grab,” Snell said of the groin tightness that ended up taking him out of the Dodgers’ 6-2 loss to the Reds early. “So I was like, ‘Alright, let’s see what we can do.’”
With Snell guiding the ball without driving hard off his back leg, his velocity was down a tick or two through a 19-pitch first inning. He gave up one hit, a single to Sal Stewart, which he quickly erased with a successful pick-off that caught Stewart in an inning-ending run-down.
“I was going to try to get through five [innings],” he said, “but I just knew I didn’t really have a good shot at doing that and remaining healthy.”
In a conversation with manager Dave Roberts, pitching coach Mark Prior and head athletic trainer Thomas Albert, they all agreed the best course of action would be to pull Snell from the game. Right-handed reliever Blake Treinen replaced him in the second inning.
With only 10 games left in the season, it’s unclear when Snell will be ready to pitch again.
“The next couple days are really going to decide,” Snell said. “But I’d love to throw on my next [scheduled start day]. Either there or a couple days after. But definitely, I want to try to get one more in the regular season.”
Teoscar Hernández’s two-run homer Tuesday in the Dodgers’ win against the Reds was his second home run in as many nights.
The Dodgers’ loss marked Snell’s eighth start of the season. His 2026 debut was delayed by shoulder fatigue. And then after one start, he landed back on the injured list to undergo arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow.
Since returning, he hasn’t given up more than one run in a start. Through Wednesday, Snell has a 1.86 ERA. And he’s a key member of the Dodgers’ projected postseason rotation.
“I don’t think anyone can sit here right now and say what’s going to happen in the next week to 10 days,” Roberts said, noting that the team would decide whether to send him to get imaging after they returned to Los Angeles. “It’s under the, ‘I’m glad it’s not worse and we caught it early’ [category].”
Snell has a history of left groin and adductor strains. He spent time on the IL in 2021, 2022 and 2024 for such injuries. He said this injury didn’t feel nearly as severe as any of those.
“[In the past] I felt like that and then I kept pitching on two of them and strained both of them,” he said. “One was a grade one, one was a grade two. So I’m definitely happy I stopped. … I’m aware if I kept pitching, I definitely would’ve strained it. So for me to stop, that’s a first. Maybe I’m growing up. I don’t know. But that was definitely the right move. And next couple days, we’ll see where we’re at and go from there. But I think I’ll be good to go.”
The last couple years, in an effort to avoid another groin strain, Snell has incorporated Copenhagen planks into his routine, strengthening the area.
“I thought I had this thing figured out,” Snell said. “Well, technically, I still do. I didn’t strain it, so that was a good thing. … I haven’t felt it at all until that pitch in the bullpen, and I was just kind of thrown off by it. So I’ve done what I’ve needed to do to be strong and healthy. Definitely a shock to me.”
After Snell left the game, the Dodgers used six relievers to get through seven innings. They combined to give up six runs and 12 hits, including a pair of home runs.
Left-hander Kris Bubic, acquired at the trade deadline while on the IL (flexor strain, shoulder impingement), made his Dodgers debut in the eighth inning. In his first major-league appearance since mid-May, he allowed an infield single and recorded two strikeouts in a scoreless inning.
The Dodgers missed a chance to clinch the division with a win. And the Padres beat the Rockies on Wednesday to keep the division race mathematically alive.
So, the Dodgers will get another shot at champagne showers in Cincinnati Wednesday when left-hander Justin Wrobleski takes the mound. The Dodgers optioned right-hander Bobby Miller after his 2 ⅓ innings Wednesday and plan to recall righty Landon Knack, Roberts said.
The Dodgers’ pitching plans for the next couple weeks are in flux.
Though right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto and left-hander Tarik Skubal have been rounding into the best versions of themselves down the stretch, Snell’s injury is the latest to deplete the ranks.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki (right middle finger blister) has been on the IL for almost three weeks. He threw a four-inning, 48-pitch live batting practice session Wednesday, with Dermabond covering the sensitive area on his finger.
The Dodgers had planned to discuss how to deploy him when he returns from the IL, but after the game, Roberts said to “make sure guys have ample rest,” his next outing will be a start.
Sasaki would be lined up to pitch against the Padres next week.
“It’s playable,” manager Dave Roberts said of Sasaki’s blister. “And given the Dermabond, the time that he’ll have in between this next outing, the hope is that it’s dang near close to being healed.”
Right-hander Tyler Glasnow hit a rough patch in his last two starts but said his back, which sidelined him for three and a half months, “feels good.” The Dodgers sent him back to Los Angeles after the series in Miami to cut down on the number of flights he’d have to sit on before his scheduled start Friday.
“Get him home, get him acclimated to Pacific Standard Time, not have to do two legs,” Roberts said. “So Tyler feels great. He’ll be ready to go on Friday.”
Roberts reiterated after the game that he’s “not concerned with Tyler,” who came out of a bullpen session Wednesday feeling “normal.”
If the Dodgers need another spot start in the next week and a half, they have right-hander Emmet Sheehan waiting in the wings. They optioned him to triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday, in favor of an extra reliever. But over his last two major-league starts, he’s limited opponents to one run and five hits in 11 ⅔ innings.

title: Dodgers Quietly Announce Huge Dalton Rushing News
author: Simeon Kotto
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers spent Wednesday in Cincinnati wrapping up the middle of a three-game set with the Reds after taking the first two contests, including a 4-0 win on Tuesday.
While the club kept winning on the field, the bigger news coming out of the series was an update on catcher Dalton Rushing, who has been sidelined since September 5.
According to an MLB.com report on Wednesday, Rushing is working through a hitting progression.
He will not catch again this season, but he could still return as a designated hitter or other non-catching role before the regular season ends.
That possibility leaves the door open for a late-September appearance, though the Dodgers have not put a firm date on his activation.
Before the injury, Rushing had given Los Angeles a productive stretch in his second major-league season. In 78 games he hit .249 with 55 hits, 12 home runs, 36 RBIs and 37 runs scored.
Selected by the Dodgers in the second round of the 2022 draft, he is still only 25 and will turn 26 in February. Last year he also appeared in one postseason game, giving him a small but real taste of October baseball.
Rushing’s absence has been felt behind the plate, yet the Dodgers have continued to roll.
They sit first in the National League West at 92-59 through 151 games and are chasing a third straight World Series title after winning the last two.
The roster depth that has defined the franchise in recent years has allowed them to absorb the loss of a young catcher without falling out of first place.
Thursday afternoon brings the series finale against Cincinnati before the Dodgers fly home to open a weekend series with the San Francisco Giants on Friday night.
Whether Rushing can contribute as a bat-only option in those final weeks remains an open question, but the latest update at least confirms he is progressing at the plate and has not been ruled out for the remainder of the regular season.
For a club built to win now and later, even a limited return from a 25-year-old who already has 12 homers this year would be a welcome addition as the calendar turns toward October.
The Dodgers have shown they can win without him. Getting him back in some capacity would only add another layer to a lineup that has already carried them to the top of the division.

title: Tarik Skubal and the 2026 Mariners would have been wasted on each other
author: Paul Taylor
body:
So there you have it, it's official -- the Mariners have secured their first losing season since 2020, albeit that was a shortened COVID-impacted campaign of just 60 games. Irrespective, the 82 losses are their most since 2019 and based on current projections, they could finish with their second-most losses since 2013. With that wonderful benefit of hindsight, it now seems safe to proclaim they did the right thing in not pursuing Tarik Skubal ahead of the trade deadline.
To be clear, we total understand why there were suggestions from the likes of ESPN's Jeff Passan, that the Mariners should make a play for Skubal prior to the Aug. 3 deadline. He was perceived by many as the type of generational talent who could lift a rotation and by extension an entire team, even if he was going to effectively just be a two-month (or hopefully three) rental. And when the Dodgers acquired him, their return package for the Tigers had critics believing the M's missed the boat.
However, as asinine as it might initially seem to say this, we don't believe Skubal would have saved the Mariners' bacon this season. Sure they could have used the 2.52 ERA and 1.040 WHIP he's produced over eight starts for the Dodgers, but it still likely wouldn't have been enough for an M's team which has been in freefall since the last time they had a winning record. At that time in late-July they were 51-50 following a series-opening win versus the Reds, but have since gone a disappointing 19-32.
Tarik Skubal just wouldn't have been able to do enough to save the Mariners from themselves
Even if you transfer the three wins Skubal has recorded with the Dodgers over to Seattle, the Mariners would still be just 73-79 and sitting four losses back of the Astros in the division as well as the final AL wild card spot, with just 10 games remaining. Some may want to contend you could also add the three games the Dodgers won even when he wasn't tagged with the W, but they were all tense one-run games. Do you really believe an M's bullpen which ranks dead last in team ERA since the beginning of August, would have come through for the team?
In that respect, the rotation hasn't been much better, ranking 24th in team ERA over the same time period. Throw in an offense which is third-worst in runs scored per game and last in Fielding Run Value, and it all would have just been too much for Skubal to overcome, regardless of being the two-time reigning AL Cy Young winner. Despite being capable of a galvanzing impact similar to Josh Naylor last season, even this alone would have been compromised to an extent by only pitching once every five days.
The other reason trading for Skubal would have been a pure waste is the acquisition cost. As much as people believe the Dodgers got a favorable deal with the Tigers to get the southpaw, they still had to give up two top-100 prospects. Clearly the M's could have blown the Dodgers out of the water with a superior return package, but you would probably be looking at the likes of Lazaro Montes and Felnin Celesten, which even at the time would have felt like a gut punch of sorts, never mind now.
Even for Skubal himself, a trade to Seattle would have been a waste, if for no other reason than he wouldn't have gotten a chance to pad his free agent value in the playoffs. Look, we get it that plenty of Mariners fans wish the front office would be more adventurous and take risks like other teams such as the Dodgers, and Yankees. However, as bad as this season has been -- and it has been truly awful -- it would have been worse with such a big swing and miss.

Dodgers LHP Blake Snell (groin) removed from start after 1st inning
By Field Level Media
Sep 17 (Field Level Media) – Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Blake Snell was removed from Wednesday’s game in Cincinnati after one inning and replaced with reliever Blake Treinen.
The Dodgers announced that Snell left the game due to left groin tightness.
Snell struck out Dane Myers to open the bottom of the first and Elly De La Cruz lined out to center before Sal Stewart singled to left. It was the first hit Snell had allowed at Great American Ball Park since he threw a no-hitter there on Aug. 2, 2024, in a 3-0 win for the San Francisco Giants.
The left-hander then caught Stewart leaning from first base and the Reds’ runner was caught stealing to end the first inning. Treinen came on to replace Snell to start the second.
Snell had arthroscopic surgery in May to remove loose bodies in his left elbow and returned in August. He has been one of the hottest pitchers in baseball since, going 4-0 with a 1.04 ERA with 46 strikeouts in his last six starts entering Wednesday.
(–Field Level Media)

title: Dodgers’ Roki Sasaki throws simulated game – but what role awaits him?
author: Bill Plunkett
body:
CINCINNATI — Now what?
Roki Sasaki threw 48 pitches in four simulated innings to Dodgers hitters on Wednesday afternoon, testing the blister on his right hand that landed him on the injured list. He gave up a home run to Eliezer Alfonzo but otherwise “was good,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.
Sasaki threw with Dermabond on his injured finger. A surgical adhesive used to close cuts and incisions, pitchers are allowed to use it in games if their team gets permission from MLB in advance.
“He came out of it well,” Roberts said. “So we have to huddle up here and figure out what’s his role. What does it look like as we sit here on the 17th or 18th of September, whatever? So the number one most important thing is that he came out of that session well, and then now we got to figure out how to plug him in. He’s going to be important, but I just don’t know right now what role.”
Sasaki seemed destined for a bullpen role again this postseason, a role he assumed successfully last year. But the Dodgers have reason to hesitate on turning Sasaki into a reliever with Blake Snell leaving his start after just one inning on Wednesday night and Tyler Glasnow’s status.
Glasnow flew back to Los Angeles after his start in Miami. It was the second consecutive start in which Glasnow was not sharp and this time he could be seen in the dugout stretching out his back. But after the game, he said his back felt fine and Roberts said Glasnow threw a “normal” bullpen session in L.A. on Wednesday and is scheduled to make his next start on Friday night.
Sasaki is penciled in now to start during the series against the San Diego Padres in Los Angeles next week and remain a starter at least for now.
“One can argue it’s best to take down a couple starts, keep him built up, because if something does happen, he’s built up,” Roberts said. “The other side is you can assimilate him into the ’pen and get comfortable in that role – if that is the role.
“But again, I don’t want to speak out of turn and say that’s done, because it’s not.”
NO SHO
The Dodgers are about to complete their first road trip in three seasons without Shohei Ohtani. Yoshinobu Yamamoto might have missed Ohtani more than any other of his teammates.
“It’s been a weird feeling because I talk to him all the time in the clubhouse,” Yamamoto joked through his interpreter when asked about Ohtani’s absence. “All I have is Roki, but he doesn’t really talk to me.”
Back in Los Angeles, Ohtani has been receiving treatment for his knee and bicep injuries. According to Roberts, Ohtani began swinging a bat, hitting off a tee this week.
“There’s going to be a consistent build-up,” Roberts said. “Don’t know when the time of return to play is, but today was positive, and hopefully we can just keep building towards that.”
Ohtani will be eligible to be activated from the IL next Wednesday. Whether he is ready to play that day or shortly after, Roberts said the expectation is that Ohtani will return in time to play before the regular season ends on Sept. 27.
“I do,” Roberts said. “Whether it happens or not is to be determined. But I do expect him to be back to play in some regular-season games. Don’t know how many of them.”
COMING/GOING
Right-hander Edwin Diaz made his fifth rehab appearance with Triple-A Oklahoma City on Wednesday, pitching a scoreless inning to close out the Comets’ playoff berth-clinching victory. Diaz did allow a double to a fellow big-leaguer on rehab, Miguel Andujar.
Meanwhile, Edgardo Henriquez returned to Los Angeles and underwent an MRI, which confirmed the diagnosis of a “low-grade back strain,” Roberts said. He won’t be eligible to pitch again in the regular season but Roberts said the Dodgers are “hopeful” he could come back for the postseason.
Left-hander Kris Bubic was activated from the 60-day IL before Wednesday’s game and right-hander Paul Gervase was returned to OKC. In order to clear a spot on the 40-man roster for Bubic, Triple-A outfielder Ryan Ward was designated for assignment.
Right-hander Landon Knack will be added to the active roster before Thursday’s game and Bobby Miller will be returned to OKC.
ALSO
Outfield prospect Charles Davalan (the 41st pick in last year’s draft) was named MVP of the Class-A Midwest League and Great Lakes manager Jair Fernandez was named the league’s Manager of the Year. Davalan hit .292 with 24 home runs and a .937 OPS. He is scheduled to play in the Arizona Fall League, where he is expected to start testing out a possible conversion to second base.
UP NEXT
Dodgers (LHP Justin Wrobleski, 11-5, 3.78 ERA) at Reds (RHP Brady Singer, 6-14, 5.38 ERA), Thursday, 9:40 a.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM

title: Dodgers Get Big Injury Update as Shohei Ohtani 'Feeling Good'
author: Cameron Kiszla
body:
Despite dour predictions from some insiders, Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani might be back in action for the Boys in Blue sooner rather than later.
Ohtani hit off a tee on Tuesday in his bid to return from knee, arm and neck pain, issues that led to a very uncharacteristic slump in the weeks before he was placed on the injured list.
Having already been shut down as a pitcher, Ohtani has also been sidelined as a hitter, though that may not be for too much longer.
Dave Roberts shares expectations for Ohtani’s return
On Tuesday, manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani “felt good” after hitting off the tee.
“I don’t know what’s in store for tomorrow, but I know there’s going to be a consistent buildup. Don’t know when the time of return to play is, but today was positive and hopefully, we can just keep building towards that,” he said.
When asked if he expects Ohtani back during the regular season, Roberts answered with a definitive “I do.”
View this post on Instagram
“Whether it happens or not is to be determined, but I do expect him to be back to play in some regular season games,” he said. “Don’t know how many though.”
Roberts’ prediction flies in the face of at least one Dodgers insider, who predicted that the Japanese superstar was out for the rest of 2026.
The saga has also raised questions about whether Ohtani was honest with the team about his injuries, and whether the team perhaps mismanaged their superstar.
Many of those questions will only be answered with time, though if Ohtani does indeed come back this year and looks more like his old self, the criticism will likely be much quieter.
What would Shohei Ohtani’s return mean for the Dodgers?
While Ohtani’s absence hasn’t impacted the Dodgers too much this month, that could be because the Boys in Blue have one of the easier September scheduled in the National League.
In October, though, the playoffs are on, and the quality of opponent will be much higher.
Some of those likely opponents, such as the Atlanta Braves, have recently given the Dodgers fits, and a healthier Ohtani returning to the batting order would almost assuredly improve the Dodgers’ chances of winning a third straight World Series.
Ohtani’s replacement, the much-hyped prospect Josue De Paula, has flashed moments of brilliance in his first few games in the big leagues, but getting back perhaps the best baseball player ever would be a huge boost for the Dodgers, especially from a mental perspective.
Do you think Shohei Ohtani will be back this year and, if so, will it be before the playoffs begin?

title: De La Cruz pega un jonrón de 2 carreras y los Rojos aplazan festejo de Dodgers al ganar 6-2
author: Jeff Wallner
body:
Elly De La Cruz conectó un jonrón de dos carreras y los Rojos de Cincinnati, al menos de manera temporal, evitaron que los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraran el título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional con una victoria por 6-2 la noche del miércoles.
Los Dodgers (92-60) necesitaban ganar o que San Diego perdiera para conquistar su quinta corona divisional consecutiva y la 13ra en 14 temporadas. Los Padres jugaban en Colorado más tarde el miércoles.
El zurdo Blake Snell abrió por los Dodgers, pero salió del juego después de una entrada por rigidez en la ingle izquierda. Snell, quien lanzó un juego sin hits con los Gigantes en su última aparición en el Great American Ball Park, enfrentó a tres bateadores, permitió un imparable y ponchó a uno en 19 lanzamientos.
Blake Treinen tomó el relevo en la segunda entrada como el primero de seis relevistas utilizados por Los Ángeles.
Mookie Betts conectó un sencillo ante Andrew Abbott en la tercera y anotó con un doble de Will Smith para poner a los Dodgers arriba 1-0. Abbott permitió una carrera con tres hits y otorgó cinco bases por bolas en 4 2/3 entradas. Tejay Antone (3-2), el tercero de seis lanzadores de Cincinnati, consiguió el último out de la sexta.
El jonrón del dominicano De La Cruz ante Seth Halvorsen (1-2), su 28vo de la temporada, puso a los Rojos al frente 2-1 en la tercera. Fue el quinto cuadrangular de De La Cruz contra los Dodgers esta temporada, la mayor cantidad de cualquier jugador rival.
Los Dodgers dejaron a 12 corredores en base y se fueron de 11-0 con corredores en posición de anotar. ___

title: Elly De La Cruz hits 2-run HR, Reds beat Dodgers 6-2 to delay NL West title
author: JEFF WALLNER
body:
CINCINNATI (AP) — Elly De La Cruz hit a two-run homer and the Cincinnati Reds at least temporarily prevented the Los Angeles Dodgers from clinching the NL West title with a 6-2 victory on Wednesday night.
The Dodgers (92-60) needed a win or a loss by San Diego to win their fifth straight NL West crown and 13th in 14 seasons. The Padres played at Colorado later Wednesday.
Left-hander Blake Snell started for the Dodgers but departed after one inning with left groin tightness. Snell, who threw a no-hitter for the Giants in his last appearance in Great American Ball Park, faced three batters, allowing a hit with a strikeout on 19 pitches.
Blake Treinen took over in the second as the first of six relievers used by Los Angeles.
Mookie Betts singled off Andrew Abbott in the third and scored on Will Smith's double to put the Dodgers ahead 1-0. Abbott allowed a run on three hits with five walks in 4 2/3 innings. Tejay Antone (3-2), the third of six Cincinnati pitchers, got the last out of the sixth.
De La Cruz's homer off Seth Halvorsen (1-2), his 28th of the season, put the Reds ahead 2-1 in the third. It was De La Cruz's fifth longball against the Dodgers this season, most of any opposing player.
Dane Myers' homer off Bobby Miller, his seventh, extended the Reds' lead to 3-1 in the fifth.
Juan Brito's RBI single made it 4-2 in the sixth.
TJ Friedl singled with the bases loaded in the seventh to drive in two runs. Sal Stewart was thrown out at the plate by Dodgers center fielder Tommy Edman to end the inning.
The Dodgers stranded 12 runners and went 0 for 11 with runners in scoring position.
Up next
RHP Brady Singer (6-14, 5.38 ERA) will start Thursday's series finale for the Reds. The Dodgers had not announced their starter.

title: Mookie Betts tallies three singles in loss
author: George Bissell; Mookie Betts
body:
Mookie Betts went 3-for-4 with a walk in Wednesday’s loss to the Reds.

title: Blake Snell departs early and Dodgers’ rotation suddenly a question mark
author: Dylan Hernandez
body:
Shohei Ohtani’s aching right arm. Freddie Freeman’s throbbing right knee. Edwin Díaz’s disastrous form on a minor-league rehabilitation assignment.
Whatever problems surfaced in recent weeks, the Dodgers were able to convince themselves they could overcome them.
The reason: Even with Ohtani unable to pitch, they had the most talented starting rotation of this era.
Suddenly, that source of comfort is a major concern.
Blake Snell departed his start in Cincinnati on Wednesday after just one inning with what was described as a tight left groin.
Consider that Tyler Glasnow traveled directly home from Miami rather than to follow the Dodgers to Great American Ball Park for their four-game series against the Reds, and there are reasons to be worried.
Very worried.
With an inconsistent offense and combustible bullpen, the Dodgers were going to be heavily dependent on their starting pitching in the playoffs.
That rotation could now be unraveling.

The last time Snell strained his left groin was when he was pitching for the San Francisco Giants in 2024. He was sidelined for a month.
For what it’s worth, Snell is convinced this particular injury isn’t severe and plans to make his next start, according to people familiar with this situation.
“Stopped before it got too bad,” one of the people said.
Then again, weren’t similar claims once made about Ohtani?
As for Glasnow, he remains on track to pitch on Friday.
Manager Dave Roberts said Glasnow skipped the Cincinnati leg of the trip to better prepare for his starting assignment at Dodger Stadium against the San Francisco Giants.
“Get him acclimated to Pacific Standard Time,” Roberts said.
By sending Glasnow back to Los Angeles, the Dodgers spared him a three-hour flight from Miami to Cincinnati.
Glasnow was sidelined for 3 ½ months because of back problems, and Roberts intimated something could be wrong with him after his most recent start. In his last two appearances, the 6-foot-8 right-hander gave up a combined eight runs, 11 hits and seven walks in 10 innings.
The questions about Snell’s and Glasnow’s health came at a time when the rotation was coming together before the postseason.
Snell in particular was sharp after returning from an elbow cleanup that cost him three months. Before his early departure on Wednesday, Snell was 4-0 with a 1.04 earned-run average since he was activated from the injured list on Aug. 11.
Snell wasn’t the only Cy Young Award-caliber pitcher rounding into shape.
The day before Snell scaled the mound, it was Yamamoto’s turn to do so, and last year’s World Series Most Valuable Player pitched seven scoreless innings in a 4-0 win over the Reds.
The seven-inning start was the third in a row for Yamamoto, who improved his record to 14-8 and lowered his earned-run average to 2.51.
“I feel really good and I don’t have any physical problems,” Yamamoto told reporters in Japanese. “I want to treat practice each and every day with importance and go into October in the best condition.”
The opening game of the series was started by Tarik Skubal, the two-time Cy Young Award winner who was acquired from the Detroit Tigers before the trade deadline.
Skubal pitched seven scoreless innings of his own in a 4-1 victory over the Reds. In his previous start, which was also against the Reds but at Dodger Stadium, Skubal pitched 7 ⅓ innings.
“Just getting in a rhythm,” Skubal said.
Just last week, the Dodgers had a playoff rotation that would have looked to other teams like the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse.
Now, there’s a chance they could be forced to send Roki Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan to the mound in playoff games.
The Dodgers could conceivably win a championship with a rotation of Yamamoto, Skubal, Sasaki and Sheehan but that would require their offense to be productive.
How much can the Dodgers count on that, considering the physical problems Ohtani and Freeman have encountered? And how would using Sasaki as a starter instead of a reliever affect their bullpen?
Snell removed himself from his start on Wednesday so the Dodgers wouldn’t have to find out. The question is whether he did so in time. Their season depends on it.

title: Los Angeles Dodgers Get Critical Roki Sasaki Update During Reds Series
author: TJ French
body:
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 4: Roki Sasaki #11 of the Los Angeles Dodgers throws in the bullpen prior to the game against the Washington Nationals at Dodger Stadium on September 4, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Jayne Kamin-Oncea/Getty Images)
The Los Angeles Dodgers are looking to capture a sweep over the Cincinnati Reds this week.
LA has opened up a few-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the NL, and the Dodgers can clinch the NL West on Wednesday. Their pitching staff looks as dominant as it ever has, with all arms looking fully healthy… except for Roki Sasaki.
Sasaki, who has been out since the Dodgers’ series with the Braves last month, took a big step in his potential return to MLB on Wednesday during the Reds series.
According to many reports from those in Cincinnati covering the Dodgers, pitcher Roki Sasaki completed a four-inning live BP in Great American Ballpark on Wednesday.
“Roki Sasaki’s four-inning/48-pitch live session today went well, per Dave Roberts. Team is gonna huddle up now and decide if he will return as a starter or reliever. His likely playoff role is in ‘pen, but he’s also their best rotation insurance in case of any late injuries too”
GettyPHOENIX, ARIZONA – AUGUST 07: Roki Sasaki #11 of the Los Angeles Dodgers delivers a second inning pitch against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field on August 07, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. Diamondbacks won 4-3. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images)
Roki Sasaki got a blister on his finger during his last start against the Braves, which landed him on the IL.
If Dodgers fans remember correctly from last season, Roki Sasaki was one of the team’s highest-leverage bullpen arms throughout their World Series run.
LA has other arms they may go to this October, but perhaps Roki Sasaki is a pitcher who rises to the occasion in the biggest moments, which the Dodgers would like to utilize if possible.

title: Blake Snell sale con molestias en la ingle
source: El Nacional — La voz de todos
author: El Nacional
body:
Solo lanza una entrada
Blake Snell sale con molestias en la ingle
CINCINNATI, MLB.com -- El lanzador zurdo Blake Snell abandonó su apertura contra los Rojos debido a una molestia en la ingle izquierda después de lanzar solo una entrada el miércoles por la noche en el Great American Ball Park.
Snell ya sufrió una lesión similar en el pasado, perdiéndose algunos partidos en 2024 cuando jugaba con los Giants .
El lanzador diestro Blake Treinen comenzó a calentar en la parte alta de la segunda entrada y relevó a Snell en la parte baja de la misma.
Snell lanzó 19 pitcheos enfrentándose al mínimo de bateadores en la primera entrada, permitiendo un sencillo con dos outs a Sal Stewart antes de ser eliminado en un intento de robo de base. Snell lanzó ocho rectas de cuatro costuras con una velocidad promedio de 94.5 mph, 1.5 mph menos que su promedio de la temporada.
Esta temporada, Snell ha estado en la lista de lesionados dos veces. title: Lesión de Snell (ingle) altera los planes de Dodgers tras su salida prematura
author: Sonja Chen
body:
CINCINNATI -- El zurdo Blake Snell abandonó su apertura contra los Rojos debido a rigidez en la ingle izquierda, luego de lanzar apenas un inning en la derrota por 6-2 la noche del miércoles en el Great American Ball Park.
Snell tiene antecedentes de problemas similares. En 2024, cuando estaba con los Gigantes, ingresó dos veces a la lista de lesionados debido a una distensión en la ingle izquierda y otra en el aductor izquierdo. Antes de eso, también perdió tiempo de juego por lesiones en el aductor en 2021 y 2022.
El derecho Blake Treinen comenzó a calentar en la parte alta del segundo inning y relevó a Snell en la parte baja del episodio. Eso obligó a los Dodgers a recurrir de manera inesperada a un juego de bullpen, utilizando a seis relevistas un día antes de que tuvieran previsto emplear esa misma estrategia en el último encuentro de la serie en Cincinnati el jueves.
Los Dodgers llegaron al miércoles necesitando una victoria sobre los Rojos o una derrota de los Padres en Colorado para conquistar su 13er título del Oeste de la Liga Nacional en los últimos 14 años. Tras la derrota, tendrán dos cosas que seguir de cerca durante el resto de la noche: el resultado de San Diego y el estado de Snell.
Snell realizó 19 pitcheos y enfrentó al mínimo de bateadores en el primer inning. Permitió un sencillo de Sal Stewart con dos outs, pero el novato fue puesto fuera posteriormente en una jugada de viraje e intento de robo. Snell lanzó ocho rectas de cuatro costuras con una velocidad promedio de 94.5 mph, 1.5 mph por debajo de su promedio de la temporada.
Esta temporada, Snell ha estado dos veces en la lista de lesionados. Comenzó el año fuera de acción por fatiga en el hombro izquierdo y regresó a la lista de lesionados después de una apertura debido a cuerpos libres en el codo izquierdo, que fueron retirados quirúrgicamente.
Snell había estado dominante desde que regresó de la lista de lesionados el 11 de agosto, con marca de 4-0 y efectividad de 1.04 en seis aperturas antes del miércoles. No permitió más de una carrera en ninguna de esas salidas y los Dodgers ganaron todas menos una. Su ausencia se hizo sentir cuando el bullpen tuvo que encargarse de los últimos siete innings, con Seth Halvorsen, Bobby Miller y Jack Dreyer permitiendo dos carreras cada uno.

title: Edwin Díaz, bajo presión: ¿podría perder su lugar con los Dodgers?
author: Julian Castillo
body:
La irregularidad de Edwin Díaz abre la puerta a que Dodgers evalúe dejarlo fuera del roster para los playoffs.
La presión crece alrededor de Edwin Díaz en un momento especialmente delicado para los Dodgers. El relevista boricua llegó a Los Ángeles con el cartel de cerrador élite y con un contrato de tres años y $69 millones de dólares, una inversión diseñada para reforzar el último inning de un bullpen que había dejado dudas durante 2025. Sin embargo, su primera temporada en Dodger Stadium se ha alejado de ese plan.
Díaz ha tenido problemas para encontrar consistencia, salud y comando. En 16 apariciones con los Dodgers registra una efectividad de 11.85, con 18 carreras limpias permitidas en 13 innings y dos tercios, además de cuatro salvamentos desperdiciados en 11 oportunidades. En 2025, todavía con los Mets, había firmado una efectividad de 1.63 y solo había dejado escapar tres rescates en 31 oportunidades.
El panorama se volvió aún más complejo después de su última aparición en Grandes Ligas, el 17 de agosto ante los Rockies de Colorado. Díaz permitió tres carreras en un inning, con cuatro hits recibidos, y al día siguiente ingresó a la lista de lesionados por inflamación en el cuello. Ahora continúa en Triple-A con los Oklahoma City Comets, donde busca recuperar ritmo, ajustar su mecánica y convencer al club de que puede aportar en la recta final.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Edwin Díaz tuvo una salida perfecta en el triunfo agónico de los Dodgers sobre los Royals
Edwin Díaz enfrenta una presión inesperada con Dodgers
El foco está en su lugar dentro del bullpen y, más concretamente, en la posibilidad de que no llegue a ocupar nuevamente el noveno inning ni entre al roster de postemporada.
Para un pitcher de su trayectoria, la situación resulta poco habitual. Díaz fue uno de los relevistas más cotizados del último mercado de agentes libres y los Dodgers lo firmaron para aportar experiencia, ponches y seguridad en los juegos cerrados. Su llegada respondía a una necesidad clara del equipo, que buscaba una figura estable para cerrar los partidos de alto voltaje.
Los resultados, no obstante, han obligado a Los Ángeles a manejar el caso con cautela. Su recta ha perdido velocidad en comparación con temporadas anteriores y su ángulo de brazo bajó de un promedio de 19 grados en 2025 a 15 grados durante esta campaña. Esa modificación ha afectado tanto su ubicación como la efectividad de sus pitcheos, especialmente una recta que ya no genera los mismos swings fallidos.
El problema no se limita a los números. Díaz pasó cerca de tres meses fuera tras someterse a una cirugía artroscópica para retirarle cuerpos libres del codo derecho. Volvió a finales de julio, pero apenas pudo disputar algunos juegos antes de que la inflamación en el cuello lo enviara de regreso a la lista de lesionados.
Los Dodgers evalúan el roster de playoffs
De acuerdo con Ken Rosenthal, no sería descabellado que los Dodgers excluyan a Díaz de su roster de postemporada, incluso con el peso de su contrato. El razonamiento dentro de la organización sería simple, aunque duro para un relevista de su estatus. En octubre, Los Ángeles necesita llevar a sus mejores brazos disponibles, no necesariamente a los de mayor salario o trayectoria.
Dave Roberts también reconoció públicamente que Díaz necesita mostrar señales claras antes de recuperar un sitio asegurado. El manager mantiene confianza en el talento del puertorriqueño, pero ha dejado claro que el equipo necesita evidencia de que puede competir en situaciones de alta exigencia. Esa frase resume el momento del cerrador, que ya no tiene el puesto garantizado por historial ni por contrato.
La decisión tampoco se explica únicamente por la irregularidad de Díaz. Los Dodgers cuentan con alternativas en el bullpen y Tanner Scott ha asumido buena parte de las oportunidades de salvamento durante la ausencia del boricua. Scott ha convertido 21 de 24 chances de rescate y se ha establecido como la opción más frecuente para el noveno episodio.
Además,la organización ha sumado profundidad con el zurdo Kris Bubic, adquirido en la fecha límite de cambios. Bubic viene de una sólida rehabilitación, con cinco innings y dos tercios sin carreras y nueve ponches, una incorporación que amplía las variantes de Roberts para octubre.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Dodgers se desploman en Arizona: suman siete derrotas consecutivas
Oklahoma City será una prueba decisiva
La estadía de Díaz con los Oklahoma City Comets no es un trámite. Cada salida en Triple-A tiene valor en su intento por regresar a las Grandes Ligas. Aunque tuvo actuaciones sin carreras en sus primeras apariciones de rehabilitación, su presentación más reciente encendió las alarmas al permitir cinco carreras, dos hits y tres boletos en apenas dos tercios de inning.
El desafío para Díaz pasa por recuperar el comando y confianza en su repertorio. La velocidad de su recta ha rondado las 96 millas por hora, una cifra que sigue siendo competitiva, pero menor a sus estándares. En Triple-A también se ha visto una búsqueda mecánica para elevar el ángulo de su brazo y devolverle mayor vida a sus lanzamientos.
Los Dodgers no necesitan que Díaz vuelva de inmediato a la función de cerrador. Su ruta más lógica sería regresar en apariciones de menor presión, acumular innings efectivos y demostrar que puede ser una opción fiable. El contrato de $69 millones de dólares no garantiza un lugar cuando el equipo se prepara para la etapa más importante del año.

Esa modificación ha afectado tanto su ubicación como la efectividad de sus pitcheos, especialmente una recta que ya no genera los mismos swings fallidos.
El problema no se limita a los números. Díaz pasó cerca de tres meses fuera tras someterse a una cirugía artroscópica para retirarle cuerpos libres del codo derecho. Volvió a finales de julio, pero apenas pudo disputar algunos juegos antes de que la inflamación en el cuello lo enviara de regreso a la lista de lesionados.
Los Dodgers evalúan el roster de playoffs
De acuerdo con Ken Rosenthal, no sería descabellado que los Dodgers excluyan a Díaz de su roster de postemporada, incluso con el peso de su contrato. El razonamiento dentro de la organización sería simple, aunque duro para un relevista de su estatus. En octubre, Los Ángeles necesita llevar a sus mejores brazos disponibles, no necesariamente a los de mayor salario o trayectoria.
Dave Roberts también reconoció públicamente que Díaz necesita mostrar señales claras antes de recuperar un sitio asegurado. El manager mantiene confianza en el talento del puertorriqueño, pero ha dejado claro que el equipo necesita evidencia de que puede competir en situaciones de alta exigencia. Esa frase resume el momento del cerrador, que ya no tiene el puesto garantizado por historial ni por contrato.
La decisión tampoco se explica únicamente por la irregularidad de Díaz. Los Dodgers cuentan con alternativas en el bullpen y Tanner Scott ha asumido buena parte de las oportunidades de salvamento durante la ausencia del boricua. Scott ha convertido 21 de 24 chances de rescate y se ha establecido como la opción más frecuente para el noveno episodio.
Además,la organización ha sumado profundidad con el zurdo Kris Bubic, adquirido en la fecha límite de cambios. Bubic viene de una sólida rehabilitación, con cinco innings y dos tercios sin carreras y nueve ponches, una incorporación que amplía las variantes de Roberts para octubre.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Dodgers se desploman en Arizona: suman siete derrotas consecutivas
Oklahoma City será una prueba decisiva
La estadía de Díaz con los Oklahoma City Comets no es un trámite. Cada salida en Triple-A tiene valor en su intento por regresar a las Grandes Ligas. Aunque tuvo actuaciones sin carreras en sus primeras apariciones de rehabilitación, su presentación más reciente encendió las alarmas al permitir cinco carreras, dos hits y tres boletos en apenas dos tercios de inning.
El desafío para Díaz pasa por recuperar el comando y confianza en su repertorio. La velocidad de su recta ha rondado las 96 millas por hora, una cifra que sigue siendo competitiva, pero menor a sus estándares. En Triple-A también se ha visto una búsqueda mecánica para elevar el ángulo de su brazo y devolverle mayor vida a sus lanzamientos.
Los Dodgers no necesitan que Díaz vuelva de inmediato a la función de cerrador. Su ruta más lógica sería regresar en apariciones de menor presión, acumular innings efectivos y demostrar que puede ser una opción fiable. El contrato de $69 millones de dólares no garantiza un lugar cuando el equipo se prepara para la etapa más importante del año.

title: Los Angeles Dodgers Announced Dalton Rushing Update During Reds Series
author: Ben Stinar
body:
On Wednesday, the Los Angeles Dodgers are playing the third game of their series with the Cincinnati Reds in Ohio.
They have won each of the first two games in the series.
Most recently, the Dodgers won by a score of 4-0 on Tuesday.
Los Angeles Dodgers Announced Dalton Rushing Update
The Dodgers continue to play without one of their best players, as Dalton Rushing has been out since September 5.
On Wednesday, they announced the latest update on Rushing.
MLB.com wrote (on September 16): “Working through a hitting progression. He will not catch again this season, but he could return as a hitter.”
Before getting hurt, Rushing had been batting .249 with 55 hits, 12 home runs, 36 RBIs and 37 runs in 78 games.
According to the site, he could still return to the Dodgers this month.
Rushing will turn 26 in February.
Looking At Rushing
Rushing was picked in the 2nd round of the 2022 MLB Draft by the Dodgers.
He is in the middle of his second season at the MLB level.
Last season, Rushing also appeared in one playoff game.
Looking At The Dodgers Right Now
The Dodgers have won each of the last two World Series titles.
They are once again in the middle of an outstanding season.
Right now, the Dodgers are the first-place team in the National League West with a 92-59 record in 151 games.
The Dodgers will have one more game against the Reds on Thursday afternoon.
They will then return home to host the San Francisco Giants on Friday night in Los Angeles.

title: Dodgers' Dave Roberts Provides Details on Edgardo Henriquez Injury
author: Toran Flores
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers will be without relief pitcher Edgardo Henriquez for the remainder of the regular season. The 24-year-old was placed on the 15-day injured list on Sept. 14.
Henriquez’s injury was initially labeled as lower back discomfort. With further imaging and testing, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said the injury is a “low-grade back strain,” per MLB.com’s Sonja Chen.
Although Edgardo Henriquez’s regular season is over, he still remains someone that Los Angeles can get back for the postseason. Dave Roberts said that he remains “hopeful” that Henriquez can return in October.
Edgardo Henriquez’s Dominant 2026 Season
Coming off limited MLB experience, Edgardo Henriquez displayed the best pitching of his career in 2026. The high-velocity right-handed pitcher was a reliable piece of the Dodgers’ bullpen throughout the season.
In 61 appearances, Henriquez finished with a 4-1 record, 2.85 ERA, and 1.03 WHIP across 60.0 innings pitched. He also added 11 holds and two saves in the season.
Henriquez was among the hardest-throwing pitchers in the league. The 24-year-old’s fastball reached as fast as 104 miles per hour this season.
“He hit 103 mph or higher 17 times, more than any Major League pitcher not named Jacob Misiorowski (140 pitches) or Mason Miller (33 pitches). But Henriquez became more than just a hard thrower this year, developing the command and the confidence to be a leverage weapon for the Dodgers,” MLB.com’s Sonja Chen wrote.
Dodgers Still Searching For Answers on Edwin Diaz’s Status
The Los Angeles Dodgers made closer Edwin Diaz the most expensive reliever in MLB last offseason, signing him to a three-year, $69 million contract.
Diaz’s first season with the Dodgers has not been what many expected. While dealing with injuries, Diaz’s season stats include a 2-2 record, 11.85 ERA, and 2.56 WHIP across 13.2 innings pitched.
While dealing with inflammation in his neck, Edwin Diaz has remained on the injured list since Aug. 18. He has since begun a rehab assignment, with results that haven’t gone well.
The 32-year-old allowed five runs in a rehab appearance in Triple-A Oklahoma City on Sept. 13. Dave Roberts says that if Diaz’s game doesn’t improve, he could be left off the Dodgers’ postseason roster, according to The Athletic’s Fabian Ardaya.
“He needs to pitch better,” Roberts also mentioned. “I think the world of him. The baseball card looks great. But it’s like, where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that.”
Diaz made another rehab appearance on Wednesday, pitching one scoreless inning. However, he didn’t produce a swing-and-miss and gave up a double, says Ardaya.

title: Dodgers news: Roki Sasaki presents good playoff problem for Dave Roberts
author: Matty Breisch; ClutchPoints
body:
Dodgers news: Roki Sasaki presents good playoff problem for Dave Roberts appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
After being pulled from the Los Angeles Dodgers' rotation after suffering a blister on his throwing hand, Roki Sasaki has been working his way back to full strength.
Scheduled to throw a four-inning simulated live session on Wednesday instead of a normal start against the Cincinnati Reds, The California Post's Jack Harris reported that Sasaki performed well, to the point where Dave Roberts and company will have to have discussions about how best to use the second-year flame thrower when the postseason rolls around.
"Roki Sasaki's four-inning/48-pitch live session today went well, per Dave Roberts," Harris wrote. "The team is gonna huddle up now and decide if he will return as a starter or reliever. His likely playoff role is in 'pen, but he's also their best rotation insurance in case of any late injuries too."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
On one hand, Sasaki proved in 2025 that he can be a really good option out of the bullpen, where he finished multiple games for the Dodgers as a closer last October. With Edgardo Henriquez placed on IL as he tries to get healthy enough to make the playoff roster, the Dodgers really don't have an elite right-handed arm in their bullpen and could use one situationally alongside stalwart arms like Alex Vesia, Jack Dreyer, and Tanner Scott.
And yet, as LA fans know all too well, things can change in a hurry, and if injuries start stacking up once more, keeping Sasaki ready to go long might not be the worst idea either, just in case.

Related: Dodgers make official Kris Bubic roster move before Reds game

title: Dodgers’ Blake Snell exits after 19 pitches in start against Reds
author: Fabian Ardaya
body:
CINCINNATI – On a night when the Los Angeles Dodgers could clinch the National League West, they suddenly could have a major issue after two-time Cy Young winner Blake Snell exited after one inning and 19 pitches.
The Dodgers said Snell exited with left groin tightness, an area that sent Snell to the injured list in 2021, 2022 and 2024 while with the San Diego Padres and San Francisco Giants. The left-hander has taken precautions ever since in managing that part of his body, often wearing a wrap around his left leg on start days and for bullpen sessions.
Advertisement
He did not throw a pitch harder than 95.9 mph Wednesday against the Cincinnati Reds, which is below his season average of 96 mph.
Snell missed the start of the 2026 season because of lingering shoulder fatigue that had plagued him through 2025 and into last year’s World Series run. After making one brief start in May, he underwent the new “NanoNeedle” procedure to remove loose bodies from his left pitching elbow.
He has looked like his Cy Young-winning self since returning Aug. 11, allowing just four runs in 34 2/3 innings (1.04 ERA) in his six starts leading into Wednesday. Snell faced three batters in the first, working around a Sal Stewart single by picking him off successfully to end the first inning.
Blake Treinen quickly warmed up between innings and entered in Snell’s place, suddenly raising some concerns for a team that will be built around its starting pitching in October with a rotation of Snell, Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow.
This story will be updated.

title: Snell's early exit (groin) puts damper on Dodgers' plans
author: Sonja Chen
body:
Snell has a history of similar issues, twice going on the injured list with a left groin strain and a left adductor strain in 2024 when he was with the Giants. Before that, he also missed time with adductor injuries in '21 and '22.
Right-hander Blake Treinen began warming up in the top of the second inning and relieved Snell in the bottom half of the frame. It became an unscheduled bullpen game, with the Dodgers using six relievers the day before they had been planning to run a bullpen game in Thursday's finale in Cincinnati.
The Dodgers entered Wednesday needing either a win over the Reds or a Padres loss in Colorado to clinch their 13th NL West title in the past 14 years. After their loss, they'll have two things to monitor for the remainder of the evening: San Diego's outcome and Snell's status.
Snell threw 19 pitches while facing the minimum in the first inning, giving up a two-out single to Sal Stewart before the rookie was erased on a pickoff-caught stealing. Snell threw eight four-seamers with an average velocity of 94.5 mph, down 1.5 mph from his season average.
This season, Snell has been on the injured list twice. He was sidelined by left shoulder fatigue to open the year and landed back on the IL after one start with loose bodies in his left elbow, which were surgically removed.
Snell had been dominant since returning from the IL on Aug. 11, going 4-0 with a 1.04 ERA in six starts entering Wednesday. He allowed no more than one run in each of those starts, and the Dodgers won all but one of them. His absence was felt when the bullpen had to cover the final seven innings, with Seth Halvorsen, Bobby Miller and Jack Dreyer allowing two runs apiece.

title: Blake Snell leaves early due to left groin tightness
author: Jacob Macofsky
body:

title: Dodgers suffer another injury blow as Blake Snell exits with groin issue
author: Jack Harris
body:
CINCINNATI –– For all their other problems lately, the Dodgers could at least cling to the fact that the heart of their starting rotation was healthy.
On Wednesday night, that might have suddenly changed.
After just one inning and 19 pitches at Great American Ball Park against the Cincinnati Reds, left-hander Blake Snell left his start early with left groin tightness, according to the team, getting surprisingly replaced by reliever Blake Treinen at the beginning of the second.
It was not immediately clear what caused the issue, or how severe his injury was believed to be. However, one source with knowledge of the situation described Snell’s removal as “precautionary,” offering at least some early optimism that he had avoided something more serious.
Still, any concern with Snell represents a huge blow to the Dodgers, who have been resting their World Series three-peat hopes, first and foremost, on the strength of a starting rotation led by Snell, Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow.
Lately, Snell had been perhaps the stoutest of that bunch, allowing just four runs over six starts since returning from a surgical procedure in May to remove loose bodies from his elbow.
Of note: Snell was pitching on just four days’ rest Wednesday, the first time he had done that all year.
Injuries have been a recurring problem for Snell since he joined the Dodgers on a five-year, $182 million contract two offseasons ago.
He missed much of last year with a shoulder problem, though was healthy enough in the playoffs to make six outings with a 3.18 ERA en route to the club’s World Series title.
Ongoing shoulder issues sidelined him at the start of this year, before his elbow injury popped up after his first start back in early May.
Snell has had left groin injuries before. He missed more than a month in 2024 when he strained his groin while playing for the San Francisco Giants, and was out the final three weeks of the season in 2021 with an adductor groin strain with the San Diego Padres.
If he faces a similar timeline to return again now, it could put his availability for the start of the playoffs in jeopardy.
Just like that, the Dodgers injury headache has gotten that much worse.

title: Dodgers' Blake Snell Exits Wednesday's Game After First Inning in Concerning Development
author: Noah Camras; Unknown
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers left-handed pitcher Blake Snell has exited Wednesday's game against the Cincinnati Reds after one inning in a concerning development with less than two weeks to go in the regular season.
Snell pitched a scoreless first inning with one strikeout across 19 pitches. There didn't appear to be anything noticeably wrong with him during the frame, but his fastball velocity was down.
At the conclusion of the first inning, Snell went down to the clubhouse alongside team trainer Thomas Albert.
Now, he's out of the game, with right-hander Blake Treinen replacing him in the bottom of the second inning.
What is Blake Snell's Injury?
The Dodgers announced Snell was removed from the game with left groin tightness.
Manager Dave Roberts will provide a more substantial update after the game, which will include whether or not Snell will need to go on the injured list.
Dodgers Can't Afford a Blake Snell Injury Right Now
Snell opened the year on the IL as he recovered from shoulder inflammation that dated back to last year. He returned for one start in May before going right back on the IL to undergo surgery to remove loose bodies in his elbow.
He missed another three months before returning in August, and has been absolutely dominant ever since.
Entering Wednesday, Snell was 4-0 with a 1.04 ERA in six starts since coming off the IL. Including Wednesday's scoreless first inning, he has 47 strikeouts over 35.2 innings and hasn't allowed a home run in that stretch.
The Dodgers are relying on Snell and fellow superstar pitchers Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal to carry them in October. Thus, the team will hope Snell isn't dealing with anything serious moving forward.
Who Will Replace Blake Snell in Dodgers Rotation if He's Forced to Miss Time?
The Dodgers' starting rotation is dealing with an onslaught of injury concerns as the season winds down.
While the rotation is led by Yamamoto and Skubal (who underwent midseason elbow surgery while with the Detroit Tigers), behind them is a bunch of question marks.
Tyler Glasnow has struggled since returning from a nearly four-month absence due to a back injury. Justin Wrobleski has been removed from the rotation amid his forearm injury and struggles. Roki Sasaki is currently on the IL with a blister. Eric Lauer is out for the season due to an elbow injury.
Then there's Shohei Ohtani, who won't return as a pitcher this year (and may not even be 100% as a hitter).
The Dodgers recently demoted Emmet Sheehan, but could recall him if Snell goes on the IL. He was sharp over his two September starts, allowing one run over 11.2 innings.
If Snell isn't forced to miss time, the Dodgers will take a big sigh of relief knowing their superstar trio in the starting rotation is intact with October looming. If he's forced to go on the IL, though, it will be yet another massive blow in the team's chances to three-peat.

title: Dodgers History: Josue De Paula's 2027 RoY campaign would put him in legendary company
author: Katrina Stebbins
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers may have spoiled Josue De Paula's breakout game, but his monster home run against the Miami Marlins on Sunday sent a message: this kid may live up to his billing as LA's No. 1 prospect.
The Dodgers still have to figure out how they're going to fit him on the roster when Shohei Ohtani comes off the IL, but as long as his brief audition at the tail end of this season continues to go well, that should be a priority this offseason.
Maybe we're getting way ahead of ourselves here, but if the Dodgers figure out how to get him regular at-bats in 2027, we could be looking at the next in a long and storied line of Dodgers Rookie of the Year Award-winners.
The Dodgers have an MLB-leading 18, beginning, of course, with Jackie Robinson in 1947, the man the award is named after. Their latest winner was Cody Bellinger in 2017.
Sandwiched in between are franchise legends Jim Gilliam, Fernando Valenzuela, Eric Karros, and Hideo Nomo, just to name a few. De Paula could find himself in some very good company by the end of 2027.
Putting Josue De Paula's future Rookie of the Year campaign into context with other Dodgers greats
De Paula has been compared heavily to Yordan Alvarez, probably Andrew Friedman's greatest trade regret as the Dodgers' chief executive. Of the 12 position player Rookies of the Year the Dodgers have produced, none are quite the same archetype as Alvarez — David Ortiz, Kyle Schwarber-esque players who can flat-out hit.
But perhaps the most apt comparison is Mike Piazza, LA's winner in 1993. Piazza came into the league with far fewer expectations attached than De Paula, but both are defensively weaker position players with massive power potential and advanced plate discipline. De Paula has yet to strike out in the four games he's appeared in.
It would be unfair to expect the same kind of offensive production from De Paula that Piazza offered up in his rookie season, when he hit .318 with a .932 OPS, 35 homers, and 112 RBI to kick off what would become a Hall of Fame career.
But when the Dodgers, who are usually so enthused about their prospects, were all but champing at the bit to find him a place to play this season, that says a lot as to where they think his ceiling could be.

title: Teoscar Hernández homers in Dodgers' victory
author: Matthew Pouliot; Teoscar Hernández
body:
Teoscar Hernández homered in a second straight game Tuesday against the Reds.
            
                Hernández had a two-run homer off Rhett Lowder and a walk tonight. Peaking at the right time, he’s hitting .417 with four homers, 18 RBI and nine walks in his last 14 games, taking his OPS from .692 to .766.

title: Robert De Niro to Portray Dodgers Icon Tommy Lasorda in New Film About Baseball Legend's Impact and Legacy
author: Brittany Vincent
body:
Robert De Niro is in talks to play Tommy Lasorda - the Hall of Fame manager who became one of the most recognizable figures in Los Angeles Dodgers history - in a new sports film.
The two-time Oscar winner, 83, is being courted for the project, which carries the working title Tommy & Me and is being developed at Skydance Sports.
The film would mark another entry in De Niro's long list of larger-than-life real and fictional characters.
Tommy Lasorda's Legacy
Lasorda spent 71 years with the Dodgers, the longest association any person has had with the team. He began as a player in the Brooklyn era before moving through the ranks as a scout and coach. He went on to manage the club for two decades, winning two World Series titles and earning their induction into the Baseball Hall of Fame.
His connection to the team never ended. In his later years, Lasorda took on an advisory and ambassador role, scouting, mentoring and turning up at Dodger Stadium in a seat near the dugout he once ran.
He died in 2021 at 93, remembered as much for his fiery personality and devotion to the Dodgers as for his on-field success.
Casting Is Still Being Finalized
De Niro is still in negotiations for the lead role, and plot details are being kept under wraps, with no word yet on how the film will approach Lasorda's life and career, according to Deadline.
The creative team is further along. Reid Carolin, who directed the 2022 Channing Tatum film Dog and wrote Magic Mike's Last Dance, is set to direct from a script he wrote with George Gallo and Cambron Clark.
Skydance Sports' Growing Catalogue
The project fits a growing pattern for the studio. Skydance Sports has moved from documentaries into narrative films built on real sports stories, a shift that includes the Ben Affleck-directed Air and the upcoming Mr. Irrelevant.
Lasorda is a natural subject for that treatment, as he remains one of the most celebrated and quotable managers the sport has produced, while his decades in the Dodgers dugout gave the franchise some of its defining moments.
De Niro's Lengthy Career
De Niro won Academy Awards for The Godfather Part II and Raging Bull, in which he famously played boxer Jake LaMotta, and remains one of the most acclaimed actors of his generation through films including Taxi Driver and Goodfellas.
He's stayed busy well into his 80s, most recently starring in the Netflix thriller The Whisper Man.

title: 「5位なんて馬鹿げている」 山本由伸への“過小評価”に米ファン怒り「いい加減な」
author: Full-Count編集部
body:
「5位なんて馬鹿げている」 山本由伸への“過小評価”に米ファン怒り「いい加減な」
現地14日に発表された最新のサイ・ヤング賞模擬投票結果
【MLB】ドジャース 4ー0 レッズ（日本時間16日・シンシナティ）
ドジャース・山本由伸投手は15日（日本時間16日）、敵地のレッズ戦で7回91球を投げ、7奪三振2四球1安打無失点の好投で、自己最多を更新する14勝目を挙げた。防御率2.51はナ・リーグ3位に浮上。サイ・ヤング賞への期待も高まるが、MLB公式が発表した“最新結果”に対し、米ファンは不満を抱いているようだ。
MLB公式サイトは14日（同15日）に今シーズン最後となる、サイ・ヤング賞の模擬投票結果を発表した。32人の識者が上位5人を選び、1位＝5点、2位＝4点と採点していくもの。ナ・リーグの5位に入ったのが43ポイントを集めた山本だった。
寸評では、山本へのハードルが高すぎて好投しても「もはや日常のように感じてしまう」と評価。発表時点での被打率.184とWHIP0.88が怪物ジェイコブ・ミジオロウスキー（ブルワーズ）に次ぐ数字と紹介し、「確固たるエース」「出塁を許さない投手」と説明した。
今回の模擬投票結果では、1位はミジオロウスキー、2位クリス・セール（ブレーブス）、3位クリストファー・サンチェス（フィリーズ）、4位ヘスス・ルザード（フィリーズ）と続いたが、米ファンからは「まだサンチェスのほうがヤマより上だって言うのか？笑」「ヨシは（少なくとも）2位だろ」「ヤマモトはおそらくこのリーグで最高の投手だ。いい加減な評価はやめてくれ」「ヤマモトが5位なんて馬鹿げている」などと批判の声も少なくない。
投票結果の公表翌日、山本は7回1安打無失点の好投でさらに評価を高めた感もある。昨年はサイ・ヤング賞投票で3位に入ったが、果たして今季は何位になるだろうか。残りの限られた登板での活躍に期待したい。
（Full-Count編集部）

title: Dodgers' Roki Sasaki: Tosses 48-pitch bullpen Wednesday
author: RotoWire Staff
body:
Sasaki (finger) tossed 48 pitches during his live bullpen session Wednesday, Jack Harris of the California Post reports.
Sasaki's live session Wednesday came in lieu of a start that he was originally lined up for against the Reds on Thursday. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters that Sasaki's bullpen session went well, and the team will now decide whether the right-hander returns as a starter or reliever for the rest of the regular season. Sasaki figures to operate out of the bullpen during the playoffs, though he would be an option for the rotation if a spot opens up due to injury.

title: Edwin Diaz Makes His Case After Dave Roberts Questions Postseason Role
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers reliever Edwin Diaz responded to manager Dave Roberts’ postseason warning with a better outing.
Roberts was asked Monday about Diaz’s concerning Triple-A performance. He has a 12.46 ERA over 4.1 innings in his current rehab assignment due to neck inflammation.
The manager didn’t mince words about Diaz’s postseason status.
“He needs to pitch better. I think the world of him. The baseball card looks great. But it’s like, where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well,” Roberts said.
Diaz’s most concerning outing came on Sunday, when he allowed two hits, three walks, and hit a batter, allowing a total of five runs.
On Wednesday, Diaz came out to the challenge Roberts posed to improve his final line and delivered a promising outing.
He allowed one hit, a 100+ mph double, according to Baseball Savant, along with two flyouts and a groundout.
Diaz had no whiffs, which is certainly concerning for a pitcher known for swing-and-miss stuff.
On the bright side, Diaz averaged 1.6 MPH more on his fastball, and he had more induced vertical break on the slider, adding another two inches from his season average.
Where does Edwin Diaz go from here?
The OKC Comets have four games left on their schedule, meaning Diaz could make two more appearances before he needs to return to the Dodgers for additional action.
At that point, Diaz will get some chances to show the Dodgers why he should be on the playoff roster.
“We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff,” Roberts said.
“So my bet is that he will be (on the roster). But again, there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us, again, to sort of bet on. And so my bet is yes, but we still got to see something.”
Diaz’s reputation can take him far and give him the nod in a bullpen with some other question marks, but it will ultimately come down to his final outings for the Dodgers.

title: Dodgers news: Roki Sasaki's 'last check mark' revealed amid injury recovery
author: Jackson Stone; ClutchPoints
body:
Dodgers news: Roki Sasaki's 'last check mark' revealed amid injury recovery appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are currently in the stretch run of the regular season as they prepare for the MLB playoffs, which are set to get underway in a couple of weeks. The Dodgers appear likely to be the number two team in the NL behind the Milwaukee Brewers, who also finished first in the league last year.
The Dodgers have played recently without pitcher Roki Sasaki, who is on the 15-day injured list with a finger issue.
Now, the team has gotten a positive update on his status moving forward.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"Roki Sasaki is throwing a live BP in Cincinnati today. Dodgers are hoping this will be the last check mark in his recovery from a blister. TBD if they'll put him back in rotation or shift him to the bullpen once he's activated," reported Jack Harris of the California Post on X, formerly Twitter.
Sasaki is one of several stars on the Dodgers' pitching staff, one that turned up the heat at just the right time last season en route to their second straight World Series championship.
Injuries have once again played a big role for the Dodgers this season, with Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, and reigning league MVP Shohei Ohtani all missing extensive time with various issues, but Los Angeles once again seems to be getting healthy at the right time with the playoffs approaching.
Last year, the Dodgers had no problem going on the road and dispatching the Brewers in the playoffs, something they might have to do once again this time around if the two teams match up again, as many expect them to in the NLCS.
In the meantime, the Dodgers will next hit the field on Wednesday vs the Cincinnati Reds.

title: Dodgers pitcher who touched 104 mph might be done for the season
author: J P Hoornstra
body:
Edgardo Henriquez’s regular season was already effectively over once the Dodgers placed the hard-throwing pitcher on the 15-day injured list Monday with low back discomfort.
Henriquez, whose 103.6-mph fastball was the fastest pitch thrown by a Dodger since at least 2008, was diagnoesed with a low back strain. Bill Plunkett of the Southern California News Group reported Wednesday, Sept. 16, that the pitcher is “hopeful” he can return in October after getting the results of an MRI exam.
“Hopeful” and “probable” can be a world apart. In Henriquez’s case, it’s unclear whether his hope stems from the severity of his diagnosis, or from his faith that the Dodgers will play deep enough into the postseason to give him a chance to recover.
In either event, the Dodgers’ bullpen without Henriquez is a very different one than what they hoped to carry in their quest to three-peat as World Series champions.
Henriquez’s fastball touched 103.6 on June 2 in a game against the Arizona Diamondbacks, and again on Aug. 29 in a game against the Detroit Tigers.
Speed is just one facet of Henriquez’s game. His 71-to-25 strikeout-to-walk ratio, combined with only 37 hits allowed in 60 innings, gave the right-hander an at-times untouchable arsenal.
No right-handed pitcher had made more appearances for the Dodgers this season than Henriquez’s 61. Without him, manager Dave Roberts might have to get creative.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki, a starter during the regular season and a reliever during the team’s 2025 World Series run, might return in a relief role once he’s recovered from a finger blister. Edwin Diaz, who is currently on a rehab assignment of his own, struggled mightily in the closer’s role this season — but might be needed in some capacity just to get the Dodgers through to the end of the postseason.
Diaz, a three-time All-Star, had an 11.85 ERA in 16 appearances with the Dodgers before landing on the injured list with a neck injury Aug. 16.

title: Edgardo Henriquez Gets Positive MRI, Dodgers Hopeful for Postseason Return
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers key reliever Edgardo Henriquez got the official diagnosis for his lower-body injury that has him on the injured list.
Henriquez has a "low-grade" back strain, and the team is "hopeful" he'll be back for the postseason, manager Dave Roberts said.
Roberts described the MRI results as "positive," which should be a relief for fans hoping to get their best bullpen arm back in time for the playoffs.
The Dodgers placed him on the 15-day injured list, meaning that he is not eligible to return until September 29th, effectively ending his regular season.
All eyes will be on Henriquez as we look toward October, when he is expected to be a high-leverage arm, possibly even the closer if he is able to get back to pitching again soon.
Why Henriquez is so important for the Dodgers
Henriquez has a 2.62 ERA, with a 2.50 FIP. He misses the barrel of the bat, strikes out hitters, and limits home runs like one of the best relievers.
He throws triple digits, which may explain his back issue, but the pitch's movement and growing command make it a deadly weapon out of the bullpen.
While he lacks the high-leverage experience of players like Edwin Diaz and Tanner Scott, Henriquez carries himself confidently and exudes a strong presence whenever he takes the mound.
It is unclear how quickly the Dodgers will pull the trigger on Henriquez in the playoffs for a high-leverage role, but given what he has proven this year, they will try to lean on him as much as his health permits.

title: Max Muncy Out of Dodgers Lineup Against Reds Due to Lefty Pitching Matchup
author: Xavier Constantino
body:
Max Muncy is out of the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup for Wednesday's game against the Cincinnati Reds, and the move didn't come as a surprise. Dave Roberts already said as much a day earlier.
The Dodgers manager told reporters Tuesday night that Muncy, infielder Alex Freeland, and outfielder Josue De Paula weren't expected to start Wednesday, according to DodgerBlue on X.com.
The reasoning behind the move is that Andrew Abbott is scheduled to start for the Reds, a lefty with a 6-11 record and a 4.78 ERA this season. All three batters are left-handed hitters who have struggled against left-handed pitching.
We will probably have to remind everyone tomorrow, but Dave Roberts already said Max Muncy, Alex Freeland and Josue De Paula aren’t expected to be in the lineup.
— Dodger Blue (@DodgerBlue1958) September 16, 2026
Muncy has hit .222 against left-handed pitching over his career, compared to .235 against right-handers. Ironically, this season, Muncy has hit better against pitching from the left side, batting .257 with six home runs and 15 RBIs versus .249 with 22 homers and 56 RBIs against the right side.
Those numbers have shaped how Roberts has deployed Muncy late in games and against certain matchups. The 36-year-old is in the middle of a bounce-back year that included his third career All-Star selection, his first since 2021.
The Dodgers enter Wednesday's game with a 92-59 record and a 10-game lead over the San Diego Padres in the National League West, needing just one more win or a Padres loss to clinch the division. The Dodgers have already locked up a playoff berth for the 14th straight season, tying the major league record with the Atlanta Braves.
While the Dodgers will be without left-handed bats, Roberts will lean on left-hander Blake Snell on the mound, giving the Dodgers the best possible matchup to attack Abbott without their top left-handed bats.

title: Dodgers DFA Outfielder Amid Josue De Paula's Pre-Playoff Surge
author: Aaron Coloma
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers designated outfielder Ryan Ward for assignment ahead of Wednesday’s game, ending his seven-year stay in the Dodgers’ organization.
To replace Ward on the 40-man roster, the Dodgers reinstated trade deadline acquisition Kris Bubic from the 60-day injured list while optioning right-hander Paul Gervase to Triple-A.
Ward, 28, made his MLB debut with the Dodgers this season, but his time in the organization goes well beyond the 20 games he played for the team this season.
He begun making headlines during the 2025 season for his unbelievable performances in Triple-A, with many calling for him to replace outfielder Michael Conforto, who struggled during his one-year tenure in Los Angeles.
Ward won the Pacific Coast League MVP in 2025, hitting 36 homers and driving in 122 runs over the course of 143 games, posting a career-high .937 OPS. He hadn’t appeared in MLB since June prior to his DFA.
Why Did the Dodgers Choose to DFA Ward Over a Pitcher?
While the Dodgers have plenty of pitchers on their 40-man roster, especially some who haven’t performed up to MLB standards this season, so why DFA Ward?
The decision likely comes due to Ward’s positional redundancy. A left-handed outfielder, which the Dodgers have plenty of—especially after calling up Josue De Paula directly from Double-A last week.
The Dodgers view De Paula as the future and already have him in MLB, which effectively put the nail in the coffin for Ward’s time with the Dodgers.
De Paula, the Dodgers’ top prospect, only has five MLB games under his belt, but is turning heads across the league already. He has a homer and three RBIs to go with five walks and a .797 OPS across his five appearances.
How Did Ryan Ward Perform in the Majors?
Ward had a decent year in the majors for the Dodgers, but not quite up to his standards in Triple-A. Through his 20 games, he stepped up to the plate 60 times and posted a .738 OPS.
He hit three homers over the course of those games, driving in 12 runs, though his OPS sat below .300 for all of the final 12 games with the Dodgers.
The 28-year-old got off to a good start with the Dodgers when they called him up for two games in April, logging two hits in his debut and driving in his first MLB RBI.
He came back at the end of May, hitting his first career home run against the Philadelphia Phillies, the. crushed another one against the Los Angeles Angels a few days later. Ward rode a five-game hit streak from June 4-10, but struggled to put up results for the remainder of the year. He logged just four hits over the following 11 games.
Ward returned to the minors at the end of June and had a decent couple of months, but a September slump may have cost him his spot on the 40-man roster. Since Sept. 1, Ward had a .191 batting average with a .565 OPS, hitting just one home run in a hitter-friendly league.
LA can still keep Ward if he clears waivers, but the probability of teams passing on a player with his track record is extremely low.
